full_text:
Nasruddin was leading his donkey to the bazaar. A passerby said: "Mulla, that donkey's tail is much too long; it looks untidy!" Nasruddin took his shears and snipped off half the tail.

A little further, an old woman scolded: "Shame on you! You cut the poor beast's tail so short it cannot brush away the flies!" Nasruddin tried to tie the severed hairs back on.

Another man laughed: "Look at that ridiculous patchwork tail!"

Nasruddin threw his hands in the air: "If a man listens to every fool in the marketplace, he will end up cutting off his own ears to please the crowd!"
moral: Trying to please every critic in the crowd leads only to losing one's head.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Donkey's Tail"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?

By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
